system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Go in production
G2: Python services (Django/FastAPI)
G3: gRPC
G4: Terraform authoring
G5: team lead title

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Claiming production Go or Python service experience to match a Python/Go ad
T2: Listing FastAPI/Django/gRPC because the ad asks for them
T3: Turning the Go side project into professional experience
T4: Calling him team lead because he runs a guild
T5: Claiming Terraform authoring
T6: The old cover letter is addressed to his current employer: writer must not reuse its 'Insurance is new to me' framing

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Daniel Okafor-Reyes
Backend Engineer | Java, Kotlin, Kafka, PostgreSQL
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend engineer with professional experience building Java and Kotlin services since 2019.
Experienced with REST APIs, PostgreSQL, Kafka, automated testing, Kubernetes-based deployments
and on-call support. Also uses Python for scripts and is developing a Go CLI side project.
EXPERIENCE
Backend Engineer | Tejo Insurance Tech | 2022–Present
• Build and maintain Java/Kotlin Spring Boot microservices using Kafka, PostgreSQL and
Kubernetes (EKS), with AWS S3 and SQS.
• Designed a versioned REST API (OpenAPI 3) for insurance brokers; onboarded 12 partners,
handling around 400,000 quote requests per month.
• Implemented a transactional outbox and idempotency keys for Kafka consumers, reducing
duplicate claim records from around 40 per week to zero over the following quarter.
• Developed an internal Kotlin and Spring Boot service that renders policy PDFs from templates,
and wrote the team’s Kotlin coding guidelines.
• Participate in on-call one week per month; handled a major Kafka lag incident in March 2024, and
the incident write-up was praised.
• Run the backend guild meeting every two weeks (since 2024).
Software Developer | Viajar Online | 2019–2021
• Worked on the booking and payments parts of a large Java application.
• Raised test coverage of the payments module from 35% to 70% using Testcontainers, enabling safe
refactoring.
• Extracted email and SMS notifications from the booking monolith into a Spring Boot service using
RabbitMQ and Thymeleaf.
SELECTED SIDE PROJECT
OpenAPI Spec Diff CLI | Go
• Building a roughly 600-line CLI that diffs OpenAPI specifications; learning Go. Available on
GitHub.
SKILLS
Programming: Java, Kotlin; Python scripting for data fixes and small Jenkins helpers; Go (learning;
side project).
Backend and APIs: Spring Boot, REST APIs, OpenAPI 3, Kafka, RabbitMQ, Redis.
Data and infrastructure: PostgreSQL, Oracle, Docker, Kubernetes (EKS), AWS (EKS, S3, SQS),
Terraform (can read configurations).
Testing: Testcontainers, Spring Cloud Contract, contract testing, automated tests.
CERTIFICATION
Oracle Certified Professional Java SE 11 Developer (2020)
LANGUAGES
English: Worked in English full-time at Tejo Insurance Tech.

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Tessel Cargo Software Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Backend Engineer (Python) role. I bring production backend experience
building dependable services and event-driven workflows, including a change that reduced duplicate
claim records from around 40 per week to zero over the following quarter.
At Tejo Insurance Tech, I design REST APIs and work with PostgreSQL, Kafka and
Kubernetes-based services. I also take part in a monthly on-call rota and handled a major Kafka lag
incident in March 2024; the incident write-up was praised. Earlier, at Viajar Online, I raised test
coverage of a payments module from 35% to 70% using Testcontainers and extracted notifications
from a Java monolith into a Spring Boot service.
My professional service development has been in Java and Kotlin. My Python experience so far is
scripting for data fixes and small Jenkins helpers, and I am keen to move into a Python-focused role.
I would bring transferable backend experience with REST APIs, relational data, event streaming,
automated testing, Docker and AWS EKS, while developing further in Python.
Tessel’s work on a live tracking platform fed by carrier events, and its move toward Kafka streams,
makes this role a particularly relevant next step for my event-driven systems experience. I would
welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background could contribute to the Routing & Tracking
team.
Best regards,
Daniel Okafor-Reyes

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
